_readme: Machine-readable catalog of the PRODUCT component library (mirror of components/marketing/catalog.json for the authenticated app). The PreToolUse product-screen-guard injects a digest of this file into every write/edit under app/(dashboard)/** or components/product/**, so the full expressive range is in context on every generation, not just the primitives the model happens to remember. Two kinds of entry: `components` are shared components that already exist in this repo (import them), and `template` are shapes described here but NOT packaged yet (build them to the description instead of inventing a new shape). Keep entries in sync when props change; guard lines render as `Name(props) — use`.
contract: NEVER invent a component. The catalog below is the first stop for any container, tile, card, badge, meter or chart, and it is checked BEFORE markup is written, not after. If nothing here fits, build the new component in the existing visual language (tokens, radii, TILE_TONE tints, band height, type scale) and add it to this file in the same commit. Improvising a `<Box>` with a border and a radius is a defect even when it looks acceptable: it type-checks, it passes review, and it quietly grows a second design language. `product-lint` blocks the interactive form of this.

Before rendering a value, ask which catalog entry is the right shape for it. A counter set, a ratio, a share and a series each have a component — a run-on sentence of numbers is a defect, not a style.

Never invent a chart to fill space. A visual earns its place only when it answers a question the user actually asks, and only on data the payload already carries. Vanity metrics and decorative charts are forbidden (.claude/rules/app-ux.md).
Never hand-roll a shape that exists here. If the nearest entry does not fit, extend it (a prop, a mode) or build the `template` shape it describes, rather than writing a one-off.
Red is reserved for risk and failure. Commercial ceilings, queues and declines use `attention` (accent-3) — see usage-meter for the precedent.
Type scale: body1 14px, body2 12px, subtitle2 14px semibold, h5 18px, h4 20px. `caption` is below 12px — never for informative text.

tones.rule: Icon containers use TILE_TONE (bg-{tone}-light/10 + text-{tone}), tones primary | secondary | accent-1..4. Bars and meters use the UsageMeter vocabulary: primary | secondary | attention | empty. Status labels use the pastel badge, never colour alone.

components.name: EmptyState
components.props: icon, illustration? (an @/icons/illustrations/* element), title, description?, action?, secondaryAction?, className?, titleAs?, layout? (stack | row), framed?
components.use: Every zero-data view: icon + why it is empty + the ONE next action. Never a bare 'no data'. Inside a card whose title is the h2, pass titleAs="h3". A section with nothing in it is never left as empty space (the owner, 2026-11-09): give it an `illustration` (the template's line drawings in @/icons/illustrations, in the secondary hue), `layout="row"` for a short band (a board, a card across the page) and `framed={false}` inside a card. Pick the drawing by the subject: launch for the first case, documentation for the court and papers, performance for goals, support for conversations, configure for deadlines and time.

components.name: PageHeader
components.props: title, crumbs[{label,href?}], description? (behind the i), detail? (a line of state or data), chip?, action?
components.use: The title block of every member screen: the page's ONE <h1>, breadcrumbs back to the home, at most one action. What the screen is for goes behind the "i" beside the title (`description`, 200 characters at most, kept by hint-budget.test.ts), never a paragraph read on every visit (the owner, 2026-11-09); `detail` is one line in sight only for state or data that tells the page apart (the kind of a case, who a passenger is); `chip` says where the page's subject stands beside its title. Never hand-write an h1 + Breadcrumbs pair again.

components.name: UsageMeter
components.props: headline, caption?, segments[{key,label,value,display,tone}], ariaLabel
components.use: A consumption readout — used vs remaining, with each pool NAMED. Use for any x-of-y allowance (minutes, quota). Beats a plain progress bar when the pools differ in nature (cycle vs purchased).

components.name: MetricBars
components.props: items[{key,label,value,tone?,hint?,action?}], total?, spacing?, whole?
components.use: Two to six counters that describe one population (a status funnel, accepted/edited/rejected, failures by stage). Replaces a sentence of counts. Port of the template's Application Status. `whole={false}` is for counters that share no whole (what a dossier holds): the same rows with no bar and no share.

components.name: TrendSparkline
components.props: label, data[], plotType?, formatValue?, caption?, tone?
components.use: A SERIES the payload already carries: value + change against the previous point + the curve. Never synthesize a series to decorate. Port of the template's stat-with-sparkline. The text is the accessible reading (the change is spelled out for screen readers) and the drawing is hidden from assistive technology; only the triangle carries the hue, because accent tones fail contrast as small text.

components.name: StatTile
components.props: href | onClick+pressed | neither (plain readout), icon, tone, label, value, hint?
components.use: A counter as a tile: tinted icon band (h-[4.5rem]) + label + value in h5, four across. `href` makes it a link; `onClick`+`pressed` make it a real filter button with aria-pressed. Port of dashboard-analytics-stats. A filter row is THIS, never a hand-written Box.

components.name: NumberCard
components.props: icon (size medium), tone, label, value (already written: countText), comparison? ({ delta: '+9%' | null, same: 'igual', hoped, text: 'vs 1 a 7 de outubro: 287' }), hint?, onClick+pressed | href | neither
components.use: A list's big number with what it was in the same span before (the screen pattern after ADVBox, approved by the owner on 2026-11-07): the icon of what it counts beside a short label, the number, and under it the move and what it is compared with, the card opening the list it counts. Compare only with the same span (the same days of the month before, the end of the same day): a few days against a whole month is a false move. The move is green only when it is the one the card hopes for (more cases filed); any other move is grey, never red. The numbers and moves come from `lib/numbers/compare.ts` (compared, deltaText, isHoped, countText). Two across on a phone, the icon hidden there. The home's tiles stay StatTile.

components.name: QuickActionTile
components.props: href?, icon, tone, title, description?, eyebrow?, outlined?, badge?, label?
components.use: A shortcut: full-height tinted icon column (w-16) + title. Four across, never two columns. A tile is its icon and its name (the owner, 2026-11-09): a line under it only when it says a state, never one that repeats the name in other words. A badge (StatusChip) beside the title names a state; no href is a readout. `eyebrow` is the template's hero tile: a small grey line over the title (its kind or state) and no description; `outlined` swaps the shadow for a hairline, for a tile inside another card (HomeHero).

components.name: TILE_TONE
components.props: TILE_TONE[tone] -> { bg, text }
components.use: The only source of icon-container tinting. Never hand-write bg-primary/10 — the template tint is bg-{tone}-light/10.

components.name: ConfirmActionDialog
components.props: title, intro?, consequences[], stays?, staysTitle?, reasonLabel?, reasonPlaceholder?, reasonHelp?, reasonMinLength?, confirmLabel, tone?, onConfirm(reason)->Promise<string|null>, onClose
components.use: Any operator action that changes someone else's account. It forces the three things a confirmation owes the reader: what the action DOES (`consequences`), what it deliberately does NOT do (`stays` — half the risk is assuming it reaches further), and a stated reason for the audit trail. Mount it conditionally with a `key` so it never changes identity on the way out. Never ship a destructive action on a bare click.

components.name: InfoHint
components.props: label, placement?, className?
components.use: What a title, a number or a chip is, behind an "i" a person opens when they want (a bare Tooltip on a non-focusable Box disappears on touch and for keyboards; this is a real button). 200 characters at most. PageHeader, CardTitle, CollapsibleCard and SectionTitle draw it themselves from their `description`. Never for what must be read before acting (a consequence, a legal note, that ONE may err): that stays in sight.

components.name: StatusChip
components.props: label, tone? (neutral | primary | positive | attention | info | danger), icon? (a mark before the words, as the spinner of work under way, said by the words too), className?
components.use: A lifecycle state as a NAMED badge: a module version (rascunho, publicada, retirada), a meeting, a roadmap item, a subscription, a lead. The template's tiny pastel button rendered as a span (no focus, reads as text). The tone tints the badge and the word is always text-primary, because the pastel label in the tone itself fails contrast on this palette. Never colour alone, never an outlined Chip for a state.

components.name: CornerTag
components.props: label? (a word or two) | icon? (a mark in place of the words, as a lock), tone? (the StatusChip tones), placement? (icon | edge), className?
components.use: A short state that floats over the corner of what it marks, as the count on the bell of the header (the owner, 2026-11-07): a menu item still to come ("Em breve"), a lock on what the account did not contract, a "Novo" on a tab. It takes no room of the words beside it, so a name keeps its line: an inline chip beside a name in a narrow column broke the module names of the menu into two lines. `icon` floats it off the top right corner of an icon, inside a `relative` wrapper of the icon; `edge` over the top edge of a wide element, near its right corner (a menu item, a card, a tab). Drawn for the eye only: the element it marks says the same in its own name ("Direito Previdenciário, Em breve"). Where the state already has a line of its own (a tile's eyebrow), keep it there; a state the person must act on is a StatusChip in view, never a tag over a corner.

components.name: CardTitle
components.props: id, icon, tone? (TileTone), title, description? (behind the i), detail? (a line in sight), chip? (a StatusChip), actions? (QuickActions), as? (h2 | h3)
components.use: The head of a card of a screen a person works through (the owner, 2026-11-03): the icon of what the card is, on its family's tint, the title, and on the right where the card stands (a StatusChip) and what it keeps one click away (QuickActions). What the card is for goes behind the "i" beside the title (`description`, 200 characters at most), never a paragraph under it (the owner, 2026-11-09); `detail` is the one line in sight, only for state or data (how many a list shows, a phone number) or what must be read before acting (a consequence, a client's instructions). A person tells the cards apart, and sees which one asks for something, before reading any of them. Cards of a CollapsibleCard group keep that component's header.

components.name: SectionTitle
components.props: id, title, description? (behind the i), chip?, action?, as? (h2 | h3 | h4), variant? (h5 | h6 | subtitle1 | subtitle2)
components.use: The heading of a section of a page that is not a card (a board, a row of numbers, a group of tiles): its title, what it is behind the "i" beside it, where it stands (a StatusChip) and its own action at the right. Never an h2 with a paragraph under it (the owner, 2026-11-09). A card's head is CardTitle. A section inside a card takes the card's sub-heading style, variant="subtitle2" and as="h3", with what it is behind the same "i" (the case's cards, 2026-11-10).

components.name: StateLine
components.props: tone (done | waiting | attention | failed | info), children, status?, action?, icon?, emphasis?
components.use: Where ONE thing stands, in a sentence, with an icon in the colour of its state: done (the success green, a check), waiting (the palette's amber, a clock: under way, nobody needs to act), attention (accent-3, an exclamation: a person should look or act), failed (red, kept for a failure), info (grey, only said). The words keep the text colours, so the state reads from them too. `status` is the state in its own words at the end of the line, so the states of a list line up on the right and stay on the line on a phone ('Aceito', 'Em conferência'); `action` is the one thing the line asks for, beside it (a document that has not arrived: its send button); `icon` names what the line is about (a phone for the WhatsApp) in the state's colour; `emphasis` boxes the line on its tint when it is the card's answer ('Os documentos de que o escritório precisa já chegaram. Não precisa enviar de novo.'), the same box ProgressNow draws for a way of several steps. Things listed with their states are StateLines, never plain sentences.

components.name: QuickActions
components.props: label, actions[{key, label, icon?, onClick, disabled?}], icon?, text?, align? (left | right)
components.use: What a card keeps out of sight, one click away (the owner, 2026-11-03): a request already fulfilled that may be made again (another copy of a document that arrived and serves, a boarding pass, a new link), or what a person seldom needs. An icon button with its name on hover (with `text`, words beside the icon, for a person who would not find an icon alone: a client on a phone) opening a menu, each action with its icon. What the card asks for now stays a button of its own, in view, on the line it is about: never hide in here the only way to do the card's pending job, nor a right the person must find in plain sight (withdrawing an agreement, deleting their data).

components.name: PageSkeleton
components.props: shape? (list | record | home | cards | split | setup), numbers?, rows?, cards?
components.use: The page that is loading, drawn in the shape it will have (the screen pattern after ADVBox, approved by the owner on 2026-11-07): its title block, then its form in grey blocks inside the very cards and spacing the page uses, so nothing jumps when the content arrives. `list`: the cards of numbers (`numbers`), the bar and the rows (`rows`; `cards` when each row is a card of its own); `record`: a record's top and its cards in two columns; `home`; `split`: a list beside what is open of it; `setup`: the rail of steps beside the step; `cards`: a few cards, for any other page. Said once to assistive technology as loading, a slow pulse that is still for whoever asks for less motion. Each route's `loading.tsx` renders it in its page's shape, and the group's own catches the rest; never a spinner in the middle of the screen.

components.name: AtWorkNotice
components.props: open, long, title, text, steps[{key, state: done | doing | next, label, detail}], footer?, continueLabel, waitLabel, onContinue, onWaitMore, className?
components.use: The notice that holds a record's screen while the product works on that record (the screen pattern after ADVBox, approved by the owner on 2026-11-07): over the page under a veil, a turning ring with the product's mark, the title of what it is doing, one line of what happens (the screen comes back by itself, read again), the steps (done green with a check, under way amber with how long, what always follows grey) and when it started. Nothing closes it while the work is short; from about two minutes on (`long`) it says the work takes longer than usual and offers 'Continuar sem esperar' (focused) and 'Esperar mais'. It holds only for the product's own work, never a wait on a person, the client or a court; the screen that mounts it decides that, remembers per tab what the person went on without, and keeps it closed while the person types in a field or has another window open (the case: `casos/[id]/components/case-at-work.tsx` over `lib/cases/one-at-work.ts`). Not for the outcome of an act (OutcomeDialog) nor for a way of steps said in a card (ProgressNow).

components.name: OutcomeDialog
components.props: open, tone? (done | info), title, lines[{key, icon, text}], closeLabel, onClose
components.use: What an act a person just did changed, said whole and in front of them (the owner, 2026-11-03): an answer that binds them (an agreement given or taken back), a decision others will act on. A large icon on its tint, the title in the person's words ('Acordo registrado'), one consequence a line with its icon (what ONE follows now, where the alerts go, how to change one's mind), and one button ('Entendi'). A line of Alert at the top of the page was read past by the passenger who agreed: an act whose consequences the person must understand is confirmed here, never in an Alert or a toast. Not for the routine save of a form (the field's own state says it) nor for the beat between setup steps (StepCelebrationDialog).

components.name: SidePanel
components.props: onClose, closeLabel, title, description?, icon?, tone? (TileTone), busy?, onSubmit? (the body and the foot are one form), actions? (the foot's buttons, the main one first), note? (one quiet line at the right of the foot), wide? (a long text read and written: a model), open? (true), children
components.use: Where every registration is made (the screen pattern after ADVBox, approved by the owner on 2026-11-07): a panel that slides in at the right of the page, the page staying behind it under a veil, 540px wide and the whole screen on a phone. The head says what is made (the icon of its family on its tint, its name, one line of what happens to it), the body is the form and scrolls, the foot keeps the main button first and "Cancelar" in reach however long the form is. It opens with the focus on its first field, does not close by the veil or Escape while `busy`, and a form opened with nothing to be of yet (the "Adicionar" of the top) asks for it first, in the body (`DeadlinePanel` and `HearingPanel` take `lead`). Never a centered dialog for a registration, nor a page of its own; a confirmation of a consequence is an `OutcomeDialog` and a question with a consequence a `ConfirmActionDialog`.

components.name: HomeHero
components.props: id, title, description?, aside?, ornaments?[{key,icon,tone}] (up to six), children (the row of quick actions)
components.use: The top of a home: one wide card with the greeting and a line centred over a row of quick actions (ModulesQuickAccess inHero), dashed arcs at both sides carrying small tinted icons (decoration, aria-hidden, lg and up only). The template's AI hero. One per home, never a second header: the page's h1 stays in PageHeader.

components.name: ModulesQuickAccess
components.props: offer (ModuleOffer of lib/modules/offer.ts), inHero?
components.use: ONE's modules as the home's quick access: one QuickActionTile per module with its own icon (ModuleIcon), three across so a module's name and its state share a line, a contracted one opening its area (/modulos/<key>), one to come badged Em breve and one not contracted with a lock, both to the overview (/modulos#<key>). Never in the setup: nothing there leads away from it. Renders nothing for an empty offer. `inHero` draws only the centred row of outlined tiles for HomeHero, each saying its state in its eyebrow.

components.name: ModuleIcon
components.props: name (product_modules.icon), size?, className?, variant?
components.use: The icon that says what a module is, by the name the catalog stores, through the icon registry; a name the set does not have shows the generic module icon.

components.name: ModuleScope
components.props: path, modules (ModuleCard[]), current (key | null), keep?
components.use: Above a page of the firm's work (cases, conversations, approvals, filing, publications, deadlines, hearings): links for every module or one (?modulo=), the chosen one contained and aria-current. The page reads only what is of a case of that module.

components.name: AttentionList
components.props: id, title, description?, total, groups[{key,title,tone: danger | attention,items[{id,href,tag,title,detail?,count?,countLabel?,icon?}]}]
components.use: What holds a firm's cases until somebody acts, where a person starts the day: one card coloured by its most urgent group (danger = past its time, attention = waiting on the firm), and in it, by group, a two-column grid of outlined cards (the template's projects grid): the icon of the thing's kind on the group's tint, what it is, its kind as a StatusChip tag on the right, of which case in two lines at most, a pill with how many when more than one; the whole card one click from where it is done. The hue rides on the icon's tint and the badges, never on the words. Not for counters (StatTile) nor for a list of records to manage (DataTable).

components.name: ActivityCards
components.props: id, title, items[{key, icon (size small), tone, title, when, facts?: string[], action?{onClick? | href?}}], titleAs?: h3 (default) | div (in a page's demonstration of the product, whose words must not enter the outline)
components.use: What the product did by itself a moment ago (the few latest things, not a history): one compact outlined card each, three across from a laptop on, the whole card the way to see it (a chevron, no button): the icon of what it is about on its family tint, what it did, and under it one quiet line with when and the facts (how many times, a detail, the AI only when it was the AI). Group the same kind of thing into one card with its count. For a long history where the order is the meaning, the Timeline de atividade template.

components.name: CollapsibleCard
components.props: id, anchor?, title, titleAs? (h2 | h3), summary?, summaryClosedOnly?, chip? (a StatusChip, kept clickable above the header), description? (behind the i beside the title), detail? (in sight when open), action?, defaultOpen?, bodyClassName?, children; CollapsibleGroup around a screen of many and CollapsibleGroupToggle (Abrir/Fechar todos os cartões); CollapsibleGroup takes marks? (by card id: firm, failed, client, and working, the words of what the product does there now), looks? (by card id: the icon of its head and its tone) and words? (the words of the marks)
components.use: A card of a long screen of many cards that a person opens when they need it: the case screen, the decisions of /settings/autonomia, the secondary cards of /settings/team, the template and notice lists of /settings/connections, the tasks and tools of /admin/ai. Closed, it still says where things stand in one line (summary) and, when something there waits for a person, what (chip, a StatusChip): the screen reads as a list of where things stand. Its header is a disclosure button inside the heading (aria-expanded, aria-controls) stretched over the whole header; what the card is for sits behind the "i" beside its title (`description`, 200 characters at most), what must be read before acting is `detail`, in sight when open, and the card own action live in the body, so every closed card has the same shape. A link to the heading id (or to anchor) opens it and brings it into view. Open on arrival only where the work of the moment is, or where something waits (a pure rule, like lib/cases/sections.ts), read once so a card never opens or closes by itself; a form inside that starts over when the screen reads again is keyed itself, never the card. In a grid, a closed card beside an open one leaves a hole: give them the full width. Not for the primary card of a screen (the roster of /settings/team) nor for a short screen of two or three cards, which stay plain Cards. The head carries the icon of what the card is and what the top knows of it: a chip when something there asks the team, failed or waits for the outsider (unless the card's own chip says it), and a turning chip while the product works there. The card opens by itself when something comes to ask the team there, and closes once it is done, unless the person opened it (a click, a link to it) or is typing in it.

components.name: MessageBubble
components.props: side ('in' | 'out'), sideLabel, children, meta?, note?, className?
components.use: One message of a conversation, on the side of who said it: the person's on the left over the neutral surface, the firm's on the right over the primary tile tint. Render them as the `li` children of a `ul`. `sideLabel` says the side to a screen reader (alignment and tint are never the only carrier), `meta` is the line under the text (when, by whom, what became of it, as a StatusChip) and `note` the line above it for a message that is not an ordinary one (sent from the phone, from before the connection, a template). Never a Card per message, and never a table of messages.

components.name: ComparisonTable
components.props: caption, rowHeader, columns[{key,label,note?,highlight?}], rows[{key,label,note?,muted?,cells[{primary,secondary?,mark?}]}], footer?, legend?, className?
components.use: A few rows compared across a few columns where every cell is a figure (a metric per segment and week, the leader of each metric per week, results per segment). A real <table> with a sticky first column and a keyboard-reachable horizontal scroll. A `muted` row is set in the secondary text colour, never faded with opacity. Not for managing many rows: that is DataTable.

components.name: DataTable
components.props: rows, columns, loading, header?, actions?, filters?, noRowsOverlay, noResultsOverlay, onQuickFilterChange?, initialColumnVisibility?, enableExport?, server?{total,page,pageSize,onPageChange,onSearchChange}
components.use: The app's ONE table, and only when the job really is scan/compare/manage many rows. Put the page title in `header` and the primary action in `actions` — those slots render empty otherwise. Imports the community DataGrid: pinnedColumns needs the wrapper switched to @mui/x-data-grid-premium (installed and licensed). A list that outgrows what a browser should carry (the firm's cases) passes `server`: `rows` is then one page, paging and the search are asked of the caller, the grid sorts and filters nothing by itself, and `enableExport` stays off.

components.name: ListBar
components.props: label, viewsTitle, views[{key, label, count?, group}], view, onView, search?{label, placeholder, value, onChange, numeric?}, filter?{label, active, content, clearLabel, onClear}, sort?{label, options, value, onChange}, exporting?{label, onExport? | formats?: QuickAction[], busy?}, create?{label, onClick? | actions?: QuickAction[], disabled?}, more?{label, actions: QuickAction[]}, chips?[{key, label, onRemove}]
components.use: The same bar on every list (the screen pattern after ADVBox, approved by the owner on 2026-11-07): the ready views with how many each holds, grouped in its menu; the list's search (waits for the person to stop typing; the page asks the server in the request's body, or filters in the browser a list read whole; `numeric` for a list searched by a number); "Filtrar" (a panel of the list's own filters, which narrow every count and every view as the module does); "Ordenar"; "Exportar" only where the list really exports (`formats` when it goes to more than one, a menu of them); at the right "Novo" where a person registers in the list (`create`: one kind is one button, several a menu, the one that starts from a document first; none on a list of what ONE makes by itself) and what the list keeps out of sight (opening a record by hand, an import); under it each filter in force as a chip. Above a DataTable, pass `hideToolbar` to the table. A list that is learned once is known everywhere: never a list with its own bar of another shape.

components.name: OnboardingChecklist / ActivationProgress / SetupWizard
components.props: see each file
components.use: Steps to first value, completion drive, and progressive disclosure for long setups. Never points, badges, leaderboards or streaks.

components.name: StepCelebrationDialog
components.props: open, title, accomplished, nextTitle, nextHint?, ctaLabel, onNext, onClose
components.use: The beat BETWEEN two steps of a guided flow: names what now exists in her records and loads the next step. Competence feedback, never a token — it awards, counts and ranks nothing, so it stays on the right side of the no-points/badges/leaderboards/streaks rule. Its primary action is what advances the wizard (drive SetupWizard in controlled mode).

components.name: CheckSuggestion
components.props: answer (CheckAnswer from lib/cases/document-check), className?
components.use: What the AI read in a document of a case and suggests (accept or refuse, the reason the client would read, what the file is, the name on it, the legs of a ticket), shown where a person decides it: the case and the approval queue. It decides nothing; the card around it offers the decision. TILE_TONE icon box + StatusChip, the dedicated view of one task's answer that AnswerFields allows.

components.name: WordDownloadButton
components.props: name, text? | read?: () => Promise<string | null>, label?, ariaLabel?, disabled?, variant?
components.use: 'Baixar em Word' on a text a firm gives ONE to work with (a model of the library, the paper its clients sign, an agency's clause), where it is listed and where it is written, the platform's too: a convenience, never a step a flow needs. The .docx is written in the browser (downloadWord over textDocx, read back by the library's own reader), with the marks as they are, so the file is the model; the text is in hand or read on press, and a failure is a snackbar. The small grey text button of a row's actions, never a link to another screen.

components.name: SecondFactorPrompt
components.props: state: missing | challenge, reason?, onConfirmed
components.use: The one setup of a second factor in the app, on the screen that asks for it (the first step of the firm's setup, and the security card of /settings/security): for an account with none, one button to start, then two numbered steps, the QR on white with its key in groups of four and a copy button, and the code in the six boxes of the sign-in (VerificationCodeInput, confirmed by itself at the sixth digit, a paste taken); for a session that has not confirmed it, the code alone; once confirmed the screen goes on at the second level. A bordered neutral panel, as the Pix code at checkout, never a warning: setting it up is the step's work. In a SetupWizard the step hides its own primary until the factor is confirmed (hidePrimary), so no disabled 'Continuar' sits beside 'Confirmar'. Never a link to the security page from a flow the person would not come back from.

components.name: InvitationLink
components.props: id, label, link, copied, onCopy, copyLabel, copyAgainLabel, copiedHelp, help
components.use: The link of an invitation in the very dialog that made it (the team's, the agency's, an agency's colleague's): read-only and whole, its copy button beside it, what became of the copy under it. An invitation dialog is ONE screen (the owner, 2026-11-03): the fields, then 'Copiar link' or 'Enviar por e-mail'; once the invitation exists the fields lock, and this field shows under them with the e-mail's result, so the link is always at hand. Never a second screen of the dialog with the link alone.

components.name: ProgressSteps / ProgressNow / ProgressBar / ProgressCounts / ProgressList
components.props: ProgressSteps(steps[{key,label,state: done|current|next|stopped,when?,icon}], label, stateWords) · ProgressNow(tone: progress|done|stopped, lead, text, extra?, action?) · ProgressBar(steps, reached, state: progress|done|stopped, label) · ProgressCounts(steps[{key,label,icon,count,href,countLabel}], label) · ProgressList(rows[{key,href,title,detail?,step,steps,reached,state,label}], label); ProgressSteps working? (the step under way turns only while work is under way, default true) and href? (step to the card it is done in); ProgressNow working? (a clock in place of the spinner while the way waits for somebody)
components.use: Where something stands along its way (the owner, 2026-11-03, after the e-mail provider's domain events): ProgressSteps draws its steps in order, each with its icon, done (primary tint), under way (the palette's amber, never its red) or still to come (outline), with the day each began, across from md and one under the other on a phone; ProgressNow says under it, in a sentence, what happens now and who it is with, tinted by how the way stands, with the one action the reader may take; ProgressBar is the same way in small for a row of a list; ProgressCounts shows how many things are at each step (the home's Andamento dos casos), each step a link to its list; ProgressList is the latest few things along their way, one line each with the step in words and its ProgressBar, each a link to it, for a home where the whole list is one click further (the firm's latest cases in progress, the agency's latest passengers). Used by the case (casos/[id] journey-card, lib/cases/journey: nine steps, the court's hearing, judgment and payment read from its hearings and triaged publications), the home (inicio/cases-journey-card, firm_case_journey of 0082), the case list's stage column and the agency's trips and passenger list (modules/direito-do-passageiro/agency/journey). The timeline tells every event; this tells the few that mark the way.

components.use: Keeps a screen in step with the database while it is open: asks a light pulse every few seconds while the product works there or right after the person acted (call acted() from every write), less often otherwise, never on a hidden tab, and reads the screen again only when the mark changed. Say checkedAt as when the screen last knew it was current. One per screen, never an interval per card.

traps: MUI 9 builds a component class list as `Mui{Comp}-{variant}` + `Mui{Comp}-color{Color}`; the composed `Mui{Comp}-{variant}{Color}` of MUI 5 is gone. Both known instances are fixed: style/inputs/button.css now targets `.MuiButton-pastel.MuiButton-color{Color}`, and style/data-display/chip.css now targets `.MuiChip-outlined.MuiChip-color{Color}`. An outlined Chip therefore paints BOTH its text (from MUI emotion, matched on props) and its 1px ring (from the template, matched on classes). Before writing a selector against a composed class, check useUtilityClasses in the installed component source — TypeScript will not catch it, because a ChipClasses/ButtonClasses augmentation can declare a class the DOM never receives.
useHighlightedSparkline derives its y-axis from the data: an empty array yields -Infinity. Guard the series before rendering.
The template's `caption` variant is below 12px. Consequence text ('this is recorded with your name') belongs in body2.

An outlined Chip ring inherits the raw colour token, so it is only as legible as that token: on the light theme, error/primary/accent-* clear the 3:1 floor for a graphical object, while info (2.12:1), success (2.13:1), warning (2.51:1) and secondary (2.77:1) do not. Use colour on a Chip as reinforcement of a word that is already in the label, never as the sole carrier of the state.

A colour prop that is CONSTANT down a whole column carries no information and costs contrast: it reads as an affordance (primary) or dilutes the one signal that matters (error). Colour a Chip only where the colour VARIES with the row.

Feedback severity tokens (`--{sev}-light` / `--{sev}-dark`) hold the SAME value in the light and the dark block of design-tokens/css/common.css. A rule written as `text-{sev}-dark` for the light theme is therefore automatically wrong in the dark one, and no `dark:` variant exists to save it. Measured on the Alert: the template pairing of `bg-{sev}-light/10` + `text-{sev}-dark` reads 2.51:1 (info), 2.56:1 (success), 2.95:1 (warning) on light and 2.15:1 for error on dark, against ~9.2:1 for the inherited text. Severity belongs in the BACKGROUND and the ICON; the words keep inheriting text-primary.

The palette is written as `hsl(var(--token))` with cssVariables on. decomposeColor cannot read that and returns NaN WITHOUT throwing, so MUI never reaches its own fallback: every DERIVED colour (theme.alpha, palette.Alert.{sev}StandardBg, getContrastText) resolves to a value the browser discards. Direct references such as palette[sev].main survive — which is why an Alert icon is coloured today while its background is not. Consequence: when a template selector dies there is no native styling underneath it, and any new component that leans on a computed MUI colour is born broken and silent.

Run `npm run check:mui-classes` after touching anything under apps/web/src/style/**. It matches every `.Mui{Comp}-{slot}` against that component's own class manifest in node_modules, the only source of truth: a ChipClasses/ButtonClasses type augmentation can declare a class the DOM never emits, and that is exactly how three stylesheets accumulated dead rules nobody could see.

COLOUR ON A LABEL, MEASURED. This theme's palette is too light on six of its ten colours to carry text, and neither MUI nor the template compensates. Light theme, against the 4.5:1 floor: a FILLED surface (contained Button, filled Chip, Fab, selected ToggleButton) paints the label with `contrastText` = white, which clears only primary 4.89, accent-2 4.51, accent-4 5.22 and error 5.31 — it fails secondary 2.77, accent-1 3.77, accent-3 3.55, info 2.12, warning 2.51, success 2.13. An OUTLINED Chip does NOT rescue it: MUI paints that label `palette[color].main`, the same tone, so outlined warning is also 2.51. The pastel badge is no better (warning 2.95). Only three ways out, in order of preference: fill with one of the four colours that pass; or keep the tone in the RING and give the label `text-text-primary!` (9.79:1), which is what the alert chips of the inherited clinical-context-bar.tsx did (git show ab2e84d:apps/web/src/components/product/clinical-context-bar.tsx); or state the severity in the word and drop the colour. Never assume a variant change fixes contrast — measure it.
